issues.description: The problem statement and the reference solution use a class named Meal (see problem_statement.md UML and solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java), but the template repository does not provide a Meal implementation — it contains an empty src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java and a separate Order class (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java) which appears to model the same entity. Main.java in the template also uses Order in its commented example. This inconsistency in the entity name (Meal vs Order) and the missing Meal implementation in the template will confuse students and may lead to compilation or test failures because the exercise description, UML, and solution expect a Meal class while the starter code exposes Order instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the entity name and provided starter class consistent with the problem statement and solution. Preferred fix: replace or populate the template's src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java with a concrete Meal class (fields: name:String, ingredients:String[], constructor, getters) and update any Order usages in the template (Main comments, etc.) to use Meal. Alternatively, if Order was intended, update the problem statement and solution to consistently use Order. Ensure tests and examples reference the same class name.
